journal: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
title: Ordered Mesoporous Carbon Monoliths: CVD Nanocasting and Hydrogen Storage Properties
material_description: Monolithic carbon | mesoporous carbon monolith (Figure 7A caption: "mesoporous carbon monolith") nanocast by CVD: acetonitrile vapour in N2 over a calcined SBA-15 mesoporous silica monolith template, ramp 20 C/min to 950 C, held 3 h; silica etched with HF; mainly amorphous carbon with a small graphitic fraction; residual mass in TGA below 1 wt% (typically 0.5-0.8 wt%)
purification_method: HF etching of the silica template, then air-dried at room temperature
notes: archive: fig7a_adsorption_filled_circles.json. Figure 7A prints no symbol key; the text says both sorption branches are shown ('the desorption closely matches adsorption'). Filled circles (integer-pressure series, lower trace) are coded adsorption and open triangles (half-integer series, slightly upper trace) desorption, by the usual filled/open convention. Temperature printed as -196 C (stored 77.15 K). Basis not named by the paper: gravimetric IGA-003 (Hiden) measurement with a stated buoyancy correction ('a density of 1.5 g cm-3 for the carbon samples, and hydrogen density of 0.04 g cm-3 is used for buoyancy correction of adsorbed hydrogen'), so basis_inferred = excess by the instrumental default; skeletal_density_g_cm3 = 1.5 is that assumed carbon density, not a measured value. wt% convention not defined and no paired units. BET range: P/P0 range 0.05 to 0.2. Degassing printed as 'outgassed (10-10 bar) under heating at 200 C overnight' (10^-10 bar stored as 1e-05 Pa; 'overnight' gives no duration). H2 99.9999% additionally purified by a molecular sieve filter. Total pore volume from N2 adsorbed at P/P0 = ca. 0.99 (single point; pore_volume_method = other). Micropore surface area 156 m2/g from t-plot (micropore volume obtained by t-plot but not reported). Average pore size printed as 'ca. 38 A' (stored 3.8 nm), read from the pore size distribution (Figure 4 inset), method not stated. Synthesis: CVD nanocasting (chemical vapour deposition of acetonitrile inside the silica template); coded template_synthesis.
